headline: Roblox Crawler Takes 145GB Without Permission
lede: A crawler identifying itself as Roblox’s trellis2-data-sourcing system collected 145.5 GB of 3D models from 712 projects, including licensed and adult-content files. The affected sites blocked it and want answers about consent, licensing, and what happened to the copies.

headline: OpenAI Presents Three AI-Generated Results
lede: OpenAI is presenting three mathematical and physical results, including a claimed refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis and work touching four-dimensional quantum field theory. The announcements now enter the less glamorous phase: expert checking, formal verification, and scholarly scrutiny.

headline: AI Agents Change the Bottleneck, Not the Law
lede: Coding agents remove some onboarding costs, but they do not abolish dependencies, ambiguity, review, or integration. Brooks’s warning survives in updated form: teams may now produce the wrong answer faster, unless humans coordinate and validate the work.
pullquote: AI changes the bottleneck from managing developers to specifying and validating agents.

headline: AI Makes Haunted Houses Look Alike
lede: The handmade flyers, props, and characters of haunted attractions are being replaced by imagery that can feel generic, misleading, or accidentally offensive. Behind the scenes, technology can still sharpen effects and accessibility; out front, sameness is a poor scare.

headline: A New Paper Challenges Exponential Hardness
lede: A paper hosted by OpenAI claims that the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false, potentially unsettling a large body of conditional complexity results. It is not a proof that P equals NP, and its extraordinary consequences make every reduction and line of the argument matter.

headline: Debian Developer Rejects Mandatory LLM Review
lede: NEW queue uploads now pass through an LLM review workflow. One Debian developer is stepping back, citing opaque tools, unreliable output, resource costs, and the absence of an opt-out; deterministic tooling remains the preferred patch.

headline: A Browser Rebuild Brings Back Encarta 95
lede: Encarta 95 Web reconstructs Microsoft’s CD-ROM encyclopedia as a static browser experience hosted on GitHub Pages. Built from Internet Archive material and documented in code, it turns a brittle technical exercise into a small act of digital preservation.

headline: Researchers Identify a Circadian Depression Subtype
lede: In a study of 11,380 participants, roughly one quarter showed a pattern linked to seasonal symptoms, delayed sleep, evening chronotype, and pronounced morning fatigue. The classification may guide circadian treatments, but validation and treatment evidence remain necessary.

headline: A From-Scratch Course Builds Reasoning Models
lede: Sebastian Raschka’s eight-part course follows a small reasoning model from pretrained Qwen3 through sampling, self-consistency, refinement, and verifiable-reward training. The work stays close to the machinery: Python, PyTorch, evaluation, and the quiet discipline of making an experiment reproducible.

headline: Windows 11 Still Runs a 1993 FreeCell
lede: A 1993 FreeCell build remains native on Windows 11 because the Win32 and NT foundations beneath it have endured. Older 16-bit programs need emulation, but the boundary still reveals an unusual historical promise: yesterday’s interfaces can remain part of today’s machine.
